text:
Treat each user’s HR@10 as a binary outcome; compare models on identical users and candidate sets. Recommended adaptation of [paired bootstrap resampling](https://aclanthology.org/W04-3250/): resample 200 users within each category, preserving model pairs, then average the four category differences equally. Report macro improvement, its 95% interval, category differences, and discordant hit counts; exact McNemar tests provide category-level paired tests. One changed hit moves category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the four datasets, fixed negatives and training seed; they exclude seed variability and negative-resampling uncertainty. Sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog rankings, so conclusions concern this benchmark specifically ([sampling analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.02263)).

Repeatedly selecting architectures and checkpoints on the same validation users creates selection optimism; ordinary bootstrap intervals do not remove it ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Recommended plan: preregister a small hypothesis list, checkpoint evaluation schedule, stopping rule, practical improvement threshold, and deterministic tie-breaking rule; count checkpoint inspections as selection opportunities. Allocate the 43,200 GPU-second budget in advance, recording failures and diagnostics, and preserve seed 42, fixed splits and candidates. Use training loss and diagnostics to screen failures; select by the stipulated macro validation HR@10, retaining simpler or cheaper configurations on ties. For prespecified comparisons, Holm correction can control multiple testing; it does not validate unrestricted adaptive search.

[Ladder/reusable-holdout research](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v37/blum15.html) motivates limiting feedback and requiring meaningful improvements, but formal guarantees require mechanisms beyond the unchanged evaluator. Freeze the selected architecture and one checkpoint per category before host-held-out evaluation; label all search-stage comparisons exploratory.
